sections.evidence:
- D05 (32 CFR part 73 definitions, "Characterization of less than honorable", L428) [c1, c2, c3]: "A characterization that is less than honorable includes a general under honorable conditions, other than honorable conditions, uncharacterized, bad-conduct discharge, dishonorable discharge, or a dismissal."
- D03 (section IV, Uncharacterized Discharges, L277) [c3]: "there are three types of uncharacterized separations: (1) entry level separation; (2) void enlistment or induction; and (3) dropped from the rolls."
- D03 (section IV, L277) [c3]: "this rulemaking does not apply to this type of uncharacterized separation"
- D03 (section IV, L277) [c3]: "Void enlistments are reviewed under the factors listed in 38 CFR 3.14, and thus are also not impacted by this rulemaking."
- D03 (section IV, L279) [c3]: "These determinations are conducted in the same manner as if such former SM received an OTH discharge."
- D03 (section IV, L279) [c3]: "Accordingly, these former SMs will be favorably impacted by this rulemaking for the reasons discussed above."
- D03 (section IV, Coast Guard, L286) [c1, c2]: "this rulemaking will have the same effect on the SMs or officers who receive a BCD or OTH discharge"
- D03 (preamble, COD Process/Eligibility, L128) [c1]: "it will be able to expand VA benefits eligibility for former SMs with OTH discharges"
- D03 (preamble, section II, L68) [c1, c2]: "a case-by-case, more holistic analysis of whether a former SM who received a Bad- Conduct Discharge (BCD) or Other Than Honorable (OTH) discharge nevertheless warrants"

Rev 1 is the one focused repair of rev 0's blocking "Needs the documents" failure (user screenshot 2026-10-09: "Answerable without the documents: This question is answerable without the documents."): rev 0's VA condition (automatic acceptance of general and entry-level separations) is public regulation, 38 CFR 3.12(a) and the uncharacterized-separation paragraph, so a model could answer from memory; rev 1 rests that side on the 2024 preamble's own statements of effect. Target medium (user 2026-10-09: no Easy slot). Rev 0's quick-test survival does not carry over; rev 1 has no platform result.
- Dependency plan: Doc 5 L428 (candidates: general, OTH, uncharacterized, BCD, dishonorable, dismissal) -> Doc 3 L277-279 (uncharacterized = entry level, void enlistment, dropped from the rolls; rule does not apply / not impacted / favorably impacted) -> Doc 3 L68, L128, L245, L286 (BCD and OTH helped) -> Doc 3 L210, L244, L52 (general unaffected, dishonorable excluded, GCM discharge or dismissal a statutory bar) -> {OTH, BCD, dropped from the rolls}.
- Universe: Doc 5's six kinds with uncharacterized split by Doc 3 into three = eight candidates. In: OTH (L128 "expand VA benefits eligibility for former SMs with OTH discharges"; L68; L245; L286), BCD (L68, L245 "despite a BCD or OTH discharge", L286), dropped from the rolls (L278-279). Out: general (L210: no COD determination, "this bar is irrelevant"), entry level (L277 "this rulemaking does not apply"), void enlistment (L277 "not impacted by this rulemaking"), dishonorable (L244 "excluded from benefits eligibility"), dismissal (Doc 5 L427: court-martial characterization; Doc 3 L52 GCM statutory bar; no effect stated; L282-286 state the Coast Guard effect only for BCD or OTH). Honorable is not less than honorable (Doc 5 L428).
- Necessity: Doc 5 is the only document defining the board's less-than-honorable set and the only source placing uncharacterized separations in it (grep "less than honorable": D05 only); without it a reader using the usual sense (general, OTH, BCD, dishonorable) drops dropped-from-the-rolls separations and answers OTH and BCD. Doc 3 is the only source of the rule's effect on each separation type (grep "dropped from the rolls", "favorably": D03 only); no other document discusses the 2024 rule. sections.question: For which separations that DoD's Discharge Appeal Review Board counts as less than honorable does VA's 2024 character-of-discharge rule expand benefit eligibility?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 5, the rule's definitions, "Characterization of less than honorable"): for the Discharge Appeal Review Board, a less than honorable characterization includes a general (under honorable conditions) discharge, other than honorable (OTH) conditions, uncharacterized, a bad-conduct discharge (BCD), a dishonorable discharge and a dismissal. These are the candidates; note that uncharacterized separations are on the list.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 3, section IV, Uncharacterized Discharges): VA names the uncharacterized separations as entry level separation, void enlistment or induction, and dropped from the rolls. For entry level separations "this rulemaking does not apply"; void enlistments "are also not impacted by this rulemaking". A dropped-from-the-rolls separation is reviewed "in the same manner as if such former SM received an OTH discharge", and these former members "will be favorably impacted by this rulemaking". Keep dropped-from-the-rolls separations (component c3); drop the other two uncharacterized types.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, preamble): VA says the rule will "expand VA benefits eligibility for former SMs with OTH discharges", gives "a case-by-case, more holistic analysis" to members with a BCD or OTH discharge, and "will have the same effect on the SMs or officers who receive a BCD or OTH discharge". Keep OTH discharges (component c1) and bad-conduct discharges (component c2).
Step 4. Source input (Doc 3, preamble): for an Honorable or General discharge "VA does not conduct a COD determination and this bar is irrelevant", so the rule changes nothing for general discharges; members with a Dishonorable discharge "are excluded from benefits eligibility"; and discharge or dismissal by general court-martial has been a statutory bar since the 1944 Act, which the rule does not lift. General, dishonorable and dismissal drop out.
Step 5. Filter (Doc 5 candidates against Doc 3's statements of the rule's effect, combining the steps above): the less than honorable separations whose benefit eligibility the rule expands are OTH discharges, bad-conduct discharges and dropped-from-the-rolls separations.
Decoy: uncharacterized separations as a whole. Doc 3 mentions entry level separations and void enlistments in the same paragraph as dropped-from-the-rolls separations, but says the rule does not apply to the first and does not impact the second, so only the dropped-from-the-rolls type qualifies.
Final answer: Other than honorable discharges, bad-conduct discharges and dropped-from-the-rolls separations.
